purpose: Hand-reviewed identity merges for the person layer. His ruling 2026-08-19: keep exact-name auto-matching in the build, and add these reviewed aliases on top. Last-name + first-initial matching was measured and REJECTED as an automatic rule -- it pairs different people wherever names are commonest (see rejected[] below).

rules.evidence_required: Every merge names the evidence that ties the two sides together: a GitHub handle, an institutional email domain, or a paper whose subject is Halide itself. A shared surname and initial is never sufficient.
rules.never_a_merge_key: A placeholder or generic display name (unknown, empty, a bare first name) is never used to merge. Merging is transitive, so one bad key chains unrelated people together.
rules.reversibility: The raw git identities and the source author ids are recorded here beside the merged node, so any merge can be inspected and undone.
rules.author_names_are_not_ground_truth: The Ankit Aggarwal case proved the metadata source can alter a given name (it stored Ankita where the paper prints Ankit). So a rejection reasoned as 'different given names' is only as good as the source spelling -- check the paper's own author list before relying on one. The rejected[] entries below were judged on the source name and would repay that check if any of them ever matters.
